messages:
maria: heads up — canary p99 jumped ~3x after the runtime rollout (kernel-autoselect v2). noticed around 12:04 UTC. https://grafana.redwood/alerts/abc123 :grimacing:
perf-bot: [ALERT] service/inference.p99 > 450ms for 3m on canary cluster
devin: ugh. I pushed the hysteresis change to kernel_autoselect to avoid thrash (hysteresis=0.15). it reduced flips in staged tests but i didn't test under our small-seq workload distribution
kevin: any sign it's kv-cache prefetch interacting? last time we saw similar patterns the prefetched KV caused microbatch density to increase and push some requests into slow-path kernels
maria: profile snippet from canary host-21 (12:06):
```
rpc_latencies: p50=80ms p95=220ms p99=620ms
kv_prefetch: enabled
microbatch_size_hist: 1:62% 2:28% 4+:10%
kernel_selected: fast_kernel: 55% slow_kernel: 45%
trace: smallseq->prefetch->kernel_select(slow)
```
anya: that microbatch shift looks suspicious — more 4+ batches than usual. I bet hysteresis makes selector sticky to the slow_kernel when prefetch warms KV, so tail gets worse
dmitri: i can reproduce locally by toggling hysteresis and prefetch on a 1-2 token seq distribution. kernel flip probability spikes when both are on
kevin: recommendation: immediate backout of kernel_autoselect v2 from canary, keep prefetch as-is until we understand interactions. roll forward only after tuning hysteresis or adding load-aware microbatch cap
maria: agree. kevin can you run rollback?
kevin: rolling back to build abc123 (the pre-autoselect commit). command: `deploy rollback --service inference-runtime --to abc123 --env canary`
anya: also pausing autoscaler on canary to avoid compounding density changes: `autoscaler pause canary-inference`
deploy-bot: rollback job started (id: rb-2026-03-18-01). will post status updates
perf-bot: note: creating a short-lived alert watch to validate p95/p99 after rollback
kevin: rollback completed on canary, 12:11 UTC. verifying metrics
maria: initial numbers look better: p99 down to ~180ms at 12:14 UTC, p95 ~95ms — still watching for stabilizing trend
dmitri: i'll run a deterministic replay to measure kernel_selector distribution with and without hysteresis; dumping traces to /tmp/hysteresis-traces-193876
anya: logging an incident doc draft: please add any snippets you used to reproduce. I'll tag runtime/kv-team
kevin: follow-up plan: (1) revert canary fully to stable, (2) create a canary with hysteresis disabled and prefetch disabled, (3) run perf matrix to find safe hysteresis threshold, (4) add a microbatch cap heuristic to selector to avoid 4+ bins for smallseq-heavy traffic
maria: thanks team. nice quick rollback. will keep monitoring and open a postmortem if tails don't fully recover in the next 6 hours
perf-bot: [RESOLVED] service/inference.p99 back under threshold
maria: closing thread for now — re-open if any regressions pop up
